# The Work board

The repo page's Work block is a board with a time axis, not a table: it answers **what will
the next few days look like, where is the flow broken, and how much of it lands on a
person**. The three table views — *stuck · pending · all* — remain behind it as tabs. The
committed drawing is [mocks/repo.html](mocks/repo.html); the marks and their colours are in
[visual-identity.md](visual-identity.md).

Everything on the board is read from the issues and PRs themselves — a label, a body line, a
timestamp — or from a task declaration. Nothing is a display heuristic, and a figure the
listing does not carry is drawn as *not read*, never as 0. The board is one SVG that scales
to its container; the page fits 1280 wide with no horizontal scroll.

## The time axis

Twelve day columns: **7 back, today, 4 ahead**. The past is washed in the ledger tint, *now* is
a solid ink vertical with a mono flag (`now · Wed Sep 2 10:30 UTC`), and every day column is
ruled in ledger blue with a small tick at the repo's daily anchor (`taskScheduler.dailyHour`,
UTC) — where every scheduled thing on the board sits. Items before the left edge collapse
into a `◂` gutter note with their count and kinds (*before Aug 26: 9 PRs, 2 failure parks, 4
unpicked verifications*); items past the right edge into a `▸` note naming the date.

Four days ahead is the honest horizon: past it, every prediction is "the same daily ticks
again", and the weekly anchor is the last thing with a date. Seven days back is what gives
the task × day grid a week of record beside its predictions.

## Lanes — one per flow

**The lane is the flow**, never the task and never the kind. A lane per task hides the chain:
an approval park is nothing without the PR it holds. A lane per kind (all PRs, all items, all
issues) puts the two ends of one `Blocked-by` edge in different rows, and the edge is the
whole point. So a row is one connected component of the edge graph — `Blocked-by`,
`Ends-when`, `Closes #n`, `Refs #n` from a task PR to its item — and a lone item is a
component of one.

The gutter names a row by **one fact**: its head item and, for a chain, its length
(`#1583 → 2`; `growth-promote · 9 PRs`). The other ids of the chain are printed once, in the
lane beside their marks. Mid-lane text is spent only on a *finding* — `unmarked`, `no one is
scheduled to close #1317`, `after #1236` — one per row, in the serious tint; every age, count
and policy sentence is in the mark's hover title and the explore panel.

Rows are 36 px, group headers 30 px. Each group header carries its title and count on the
left and the group's **one derived sentence** in the lane, in secondary ink, nothing else.

## The four groups, and their ranking

| Group | Rows are | Ranked within by |
|---|---|---|
| **Now — waiting for you** | every open PR, each a bar from *opened* to *now*, wired to the item it ends or the issue it closes | age of the oldest PR in the row, oldest first; a row whose merge releases an edge sorts above one that releases nothing |
| **Flows — blocked, parked, waiting** | ad-hoc items and the plain issues that block them, placed at their **predicted run time** | broken lanes first (a blocker nothing is scheduled to move), then parks by park age, then sleepers by wake date |
| **Scheduled — the daily anchor** | a **task × day grid**: one row per daily task, then `weekly · N tasks` as one row | declaration order; the weekly row last |
| **Quiet** | one ruled line, not a row: the plain issues on no edge, counted by what matters (rotting, quick-win, needs-decision) | — |

Now's header sentence is the **tomorrow-workload line** (below). Flows' header says how its
rows are placed. Scheduled's header names the anchor.

### Collapse rules

- PRs from one task under one landing policy collapse into a **thick bar** with a count
  (`9 PRs · 14 d → 2 d · policy: nothing`), its left end at the oldest and a `◂` where that
  is past the edge.
- Repeated verification items collapse into **one row of stacked park marks**, with the
  unpicked ones as a `◂` note.
- A ladder of plain issues (a migration plan's phases with `Blocked-by` and no queue mark)
  collapses into one gutter note, since none of it has a time.
- Each group is **capped at its worst four rows**, followed by one `N more rows` line naming
  what it holds; the list drops open on click, as HTML below the board.
- A plain issue reaches the board only where it sits on an edge; the rest are the quiet line.

## Marks — what each is read from

| Thing | Mark and place | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| open PR | a bar from `created_at` to *now* in the machine's blue; its length is its age; `◂` past the left edge | PR listing |
| PR waiting for a person | `▲` in amber above the bar's *now* end | no `Automerge:` / `Merge:` line on the item, or the task's `automerge` is `nothing`, or the run's converge comment says `AUTOMERGE: no` |
| ad-hoc item, blocked on a date | hollow circle at its `Not-before` | body line, absolute form only |
| ad-hoc item, blocked on an issue | hollow circle **after** the blocker's predicted time; a PR blocker puts it at *now* + "when you merge"; a plain-issue blocker nothing is scheduled to close gives it **no time — the lane is drawn broken** | `Blocked-by: #n` and the blocker's own placement |
| ad-hoc item, ready | hollow circle at the next scheduler tick — the daily anchor, or the drain tick (its hour not read here) | `task:status:waiting-for-executor` |
| item on no mark | dashed hollow circle, `unmarked` beside it | a `Blocked-by` chain with no `task:origin:ad-hoc` on the link |
| park | square at *now*, the kind as the glyph inside: `×` action, `–` approval, `?` decision, hatch failure | `task:status:needs-human-<kind>` |
| running | filled circle at *now* | `task:status:running-agent` / `running-executor` |
| plain issue | diamond at the *head* of the edge it blocks: hollow ink = plain; filled good = `quick-win`; dotted outline = rotting (`updated_at` ≥ 14 d ago); ghost in the past wash = a ladder phase with no time | labels, `updated_at`, reverse `Blocked-by` |
| a relative date | flagged (`on a relative date`) in the `▸` note, never guessed | a `Not-before` in a form the parser does not read |

**Broken lane.** An edge whose upstream end is a park, a failure, or a plain issue no task and
no PR names is drawn as a dashed line in the critical hue with a `»` break, and the downstream
text says why in words. A lane is not broken because it waits: a future `Not-before` is the
mechanism working.

## The Scheduled group — a task × day grid

One row per scheduled task, one cell per day column, at the day's anchor. A cell's state is
carried by **form and the semantic set**, so it reads in either theme:

| State | Cell | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| **ran** | filled, good | a closed item of that task with `outcome:done` / `delivered`, by `closed_at` |
| **asked, declined** | hollow, muted | a closed item with `outcome:obsolete`, or the schedule board's `verdict: no` for that ask |
| **parked** | filled, amber | an open item of that task at `needs-human-approval` (it waits for a person) |
| **failure park** | hatched, critical stroke | an open item at `needs-human-failure`, placed on the day it parked; `◂` at the left edge when older than the window |
| **predicted** | hollow, the machine's blue | the next anchor for a task whose last verdict on the board was `go` or `fail-open` |
| **will decline** | **half-height** hollow, muted | the next anchor for a task whose last verdict was `no` |
| **running** | filled circle at *now* | `task:status:running-agent` |

A day with more than one occurrence carries the count *in* the cell in mono (`4`, `7`); the
hover names the tasks and their outcomes. Predicted and declined are told apart by height,
never by dash pattern, which at 3 px is invisible.

**A failure park lands on its own task's row**, followed by whatever the task did after it.
The roster reads such a park as *the lane is held — nothing new is scheduled*; a hatched cell
followed by filled cells is the record disagreeing, read left to right on one line. There is
no separate "held lanes" row, because the contradiction is a row fact.

## Tomorrow's human workload

The Now group's header sentence, derived, never a tile: **the PRs waiting now, plus the
scheduled runs whose declaration cannot land their own PR** — `automerge: 'nothing'` — plus
the runs whose policy covers only local packs and habitually write wider (currently parked on
approval). Each predicted cell of such a task carries `+1` in the lane and the row ends in
`+1 PR / day`; the sentence reads `21 open PRs · every one waits for a person · +1 a day from
growth-promote, 2–4 on Sunday`. It is the declarations' `automerge` field read against the
schedule board's `next window`, not a guess.

## The quiet tail

One ruled line under the board: `50 issues, quiet — plain, on no edge`, then three counts in
mono — **rotting** (`updated_at` ≥ 14 d), **quick-win**, **needs-decision** — and a `show ▾`
that drops the named lists with their ages. A quick-win that unblocks nothing by `Blocked-by`
is said so; a needs-decision label is a decision park by another name and is said so.

## The explore panel — per status

One click on a mark opens its panel under the board, on the same sheet below a double rule.
**One is open at rest** — the worst failure, full width — and a second opens beside it on
click; `close ×` returns to one. The contents differ by status, because the reader's next move
differs. Every panel ends in **do**: one imperative.

| Status | Panel carries | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **pending PR** | *waits for*: the policy expression and the run's own `AUTOMERGE:` sentence; *closes / ends*: the `Closes #n` or `Ends-when` target and what the queue does on merge against close; *unblocks*: reverse `Blocked-by` hits; *size · CI*: **not read** until the PR page and the head sha's checks are fetched; *left by*: the item, its model, session, claim → hand-off → converge timestamps | PR body, item body, item comments (`CLAIM_MARKER`, `HANDOFF_MARKER`, the converge comment) |
| **failed task** | *last run*: claim, nonce, session, what it delivered and the PR it left (merged?); *what broke*: the converge comment's own sentence; *park history*: which janitor rule parked it, when, whether it was re-queued or superseded, and the later runs of the same task with their outcomes; *lane*: what the roster claims against what the record shows; *do*: the `converge-item` command | item comments, closed items of the same task |
| **stuck ad-hoc item** | the chain as a list: each `Blocked-by` target with its state and *who is scheduled to move it* (a task, a PR, nobody); the janitor's stuck-dependency comment and its date; the age of the premise — `created_at` and the latest `main` commit touching the paths it names; its `Automerge:` policy as the landing it will get; *do*: close the blocker, mark it ad-hoc, or re-scope | body lines, blocker issues, janitor comment |
| **plain issue** | age and idle; *blocks*: reverse edges and, transitively, the rows it holds; *who moves it*: no mark, no `Task:` field, no PR `Closes` it; *rot*: idle against the 14 d bar and whether its premise moved (a later issue or merge naming the same subject); *quick-win*: the label, and what closing it unblocks; *do* | labels, reverse edges, PR bodies |

| **park** | approval: as pending PR (it *is* the PR); action and decision: the converge comment's ask, verbatim, and the `Ends-when` / `Retry-every` that would close it without a person | item comments, body lines |

The Work bar's tabs read **board · stuck · pending · all**, with counts in mono. The three
table views keep the rows and columns they have; the board is `workRows`'s classification
drawn in time, so *stuck* is the set of rows the board draws broken or parked, *pending* the

since an empty board teaches its reader the page is broken.

rows at all.

Start here

The one piece of work most worth doing in this repo — the top row of the same ranking the work table below is ordered by, named with the issue to open, so the block and the table are one verdict rather than two. The minutes beside it are one term of the same sum the tiles above total — the park's own rate, by what it asks of you. An approval is charged the floor of its rate, since no PR's size is read here, and work the estimate does not cover shows no figure rather than a zero.

This repo at a glance

The first two tiles are the ones that mean work has stopped and is waiting on a person; the rest are context for reading them. A tile is coloured only when it is reporting something, so a coloured tile always means look here.

Minutes is deliberately crude: every item parked for a person, at a flat 7 minutes each. Nothing here measures how long a park actually takes, and the honest way to publish a number nothing measures is to publish the assumption where you can argue with it. Drift compares this repo's stamped engine and pack versions against the canon's live ones — and reads unknown when no canon is configured, never current. Issues and pull requests are counted within the issue window, so one older than it is not counted rather than counted wrongly.

Work

One row per piece of work — every declared task, including one that has never run, plus any open item whose task this repo no longer declares. The three views are three questions, and each shows the columns its own question needs: stuck is what has stopped and how long it has been, pending is what is moving and what happens next, all is what each task is and what it has done.

Everything flagged mirrors a rule the engine will actually act on — a blown leash the next run reclaims, a dependency past the janitor's threshold, a park holding its task's lane — never a display heuristic. The page opens on the worst non-empty view, and the rows keep their identity across a switch: they move rather than being redrawn, so the row you were reading stays findable.

What the queue closed

Every occurrence is a work item, and a converged one closes wearing its outcome. Today is counted from the live issue page; the days before it come from this repo's own usage.GENERATED.json, folded hourly. A day neither source reached is left blank rather than drawn at the floor — "not read" and "nothing happened" are different facts and this chart keeps them apart.

What ran — the last 48 hours

Three different things per hour: scheduler runs (the hourly tick that decides what is due), executor runs (a dispatch actually being run), and agent sessions (a session that opened and captured). A scheduler run that fails is not a task that fails — it means nothing got to be decided at all.

The freshest hours come from the live run listing this page already fetched; the rest from the usage fold. Hover an hour for the tasks that executed in it — the run listing cannot say, since nothing in it names a task, so that detail is the fold's or it is absent.

# open; a PR keeps its merge date and the issue its body closes, never the body.
import re
CLOSES=re.compile(r'(?:^|\n)[^\S\n]*(?:closes|fixes|resolves)[^\S\n]+#(\d+)\b', re.I)
def proj_issue(i):
    return {
        'number': i['number'], 'title': i['title'], 'state': (i.get('state') or 'open').lower(),
        'labels': [l['name'] if isinstance(l, dict) else l for l in (i.get('labels') or [])],

attachment.snippet:
1	# The Work board
2	
3	The repo page's Work block is a board with a time axis, not a table: it answers **what will
4	the next few days look like, where is the flow broken, and how much of it lands on a
5	person**. The three table views — *stuck · pending · all* — remain behind it as tabs. The
6	committed drawing is [mocks/repo.html](mocks/repo.html); the marks and their colours are in
7	[visual-identity.md](visual-identity.md).
8	
9	Everything on the board is read from the issues and PRs themselves — a label, a body line, a
10	timestamp — or from a task declaration. Nothing is a display heuristic, and a figure the
11	listing does not carry is drawn as *not read*, never as 0. The board is one SVG that scales
12	to its container; the page fits 1280 wide with no horizontal scroll.
13	
14	## The time axis
15	
16	Twelve day columns: **7 back, today, 4 ahead**. The past is washed in the ledger tint, *now* is
17	a solid ink vertical with a mono flag (`now · Wed Sep 2 10:30 UTC`), and every day column is
18	ruled in ledger blue with a small tick at the repo's daily anchor (`taskScheduler.dailyHour`,
19	UTC) — where every scheduled thing on the board sits. Items before the left edge collapse
20	into a `◂` gutter note with their count and kinds (*before Aug 26: 9 PRs, 2 failure parks, 4
21	unpicked verifications*); items past the right edge into a `▸` note naming the date.
22	
23	Four days ahead is the honest horizon: past it, every prediction is "the same daily ticks
24	again", and the weekly anchor is the last thing with a date. Seven days back is what gives
25	the task × day grid a week of record beside its predictions.
26	
27	## Lanes — one per flow
28	
29	**The lane is the flow**, never the task and never the kind. A lane per task hides the chain:
30	an approval park is nothing without the PR it holds. A lane per kind (all PRs, all items, all
31	issues) puts the two ends of one `Blocked-by` edge in different rows, and the edge is the
32	whole point. So a row is one connected component of the edge graph — `Blocked-by`,
33	`Ends-when`, `Closes #n` from a task PR to its item — and a lone item is a component of one.
34	
35	`Refs #n` is **not read**: the page's PR projection parses the closing issue out of a body
36	and then drops the body, so a `Refs` edge would cost a request per PR. It is absent rather
37	than approximated, like every other field this board cannot see.
38	
39	The gutter names a row by **one fact**: its head item and, for a chain, its length
40	(`#1583 → 2`; `growth-promote · 9 PRs`). The other ids of the chain are printed once, in the
41	lane beside their marks. Mid-lane text is spent only on a *finding* — `unmarked`, `no one is
42	scheduled to close #1317`, `after #1236` — one per row, in the serious tint; every age, count
43	and policy sentence is in the mark's hover title and the explore panel.
44	
45	Rows are 36 px, group headers 30 px. Each group header carries its title and count on the
46	left and the group's **one derived sentence** in the lane, in secondary ink, nothing else.
47	
48	## The four groups, and their ranking
49	
50	| Group | Rows are | Ranked within by |
51	|---|---|---|
52	| **Now — waiting for you** | every open PR, each a bar from *opened* to *now*, wired to the item it ends or the issue it closes | age of the oldest PR in the row, oldest first; a row whose merge releases an edge sorts above one that releases nothing |
53	| **Flows — blocked, parked, waiting** | ad-hoc items and the plain issues that block them, placed at their **predicted run time** | broken lanes first (a blocker nothing is scheduled to move), then parks by park age, then sleepers by wake date |
54	| **Scheduled — the daily anchor** | a **task × day grid**: one row per daily task, then `weekly · N tasks` as one row | declaration order; the weekly row last |
55	| **Quiet** | one ruled line, not a row: the plain issues on no edge, counted by what matters (rotting, quick-win, needs-decision) | — |
56	
57	Now's header sentence is the **tomorrow-workload line** (below). Flows' header says how its
58	rows are placed. Scheduled's header names the anchor.
59	
60	### Collapse rules
61	
62	- PRs from one task under one landing policy collapse into a **thick bar** with a count
63	  (`9 PRs · 14 d → 2 d · policy: nothing`), its left end at the oldest and a `◂` where that
64	  is past the edge.
65	- Repeated verification items collapse into **one row of stacked park marks**, with the
66	  unpicked ones as a `◂` note.
67	- A ladder of plain issues (a migration plan's phases with `Blocked-by` and no queue mark)
68	  collapses into one gutter note, since none of it has a time.
69	- Each group is **capped at its worst four rows**, followed by one `N more rows` line naming
70	  what it holds; the list drops open on click, as HTML below the board.
71	- A plain issue reaches the board only where it sits on an edge; the rest are the quiet line.
72	
73	## Marks — what each is read from
74	
75	| Thing | Mark and place | Read from |
76	|---|---|---|
77	| open PR | a bar from `created_at` to *now* in the machine's blue; its length is its age; `◂` past the left edge | PR listing |
78	| PR waiting for a person | `▲` in amber above the bar's *now* end | no `Merge:` line on the item, or the task's `automerge` is `nothing`, or no work item names the PR at all; the run's own converge verdict lives in a comment the board does not fetch, so a PR whose item *does* authorize a merge reads as still open rather than as waiting |
79	| ad-hoc item, blocked on a date | hollow circle at its `Not-before` | body line, absolute form only |
80	| ad-hoc item, blocked on an issue | hollow circle **after** the blocker's predicted time; a PR blocker puts it at *now* + "when you merge"; a plain-issue blocker nothing is scheduled to close gives it **no time — the lane is drawn broken** | `Blocked-by: #n` and the blocker's own placement |
81	| ad-hoc item, ready | hollow circle at the next scheduler tick — the daily anchor, or the drain tick (its hour not read here) | `task:status:waiting-for-executor` |
82	| item on no mark | dashed hollow circle, `unmarked` beside it | a `Blocked-by` chain with no `task:origin:ad-hoc` on the link |
83	| park | square at *now*, the kind as the glyph inside: `×` action, `–` approval, `?` decision, hatch failure | `task:status:needs-human-<kind>` |
84	| running | filled circle at *now* | `task:status:running-agent` / `running-executor` |
85	| plain issue | diamond at the *head* of the edge it blocks: hollow ink = plain; filled good = `quick-win`; dotted outline = rotting (`updated_at` ≥ 14 d ago); ghost in the past wash = a ladder phase with no time | labels, `updated_at`, reverse `Blocked-by` |
86	| a relative date | flagged (`on a relative date`) in the `▸` note, never guessed | a `Not-before` in a form the parser does not read |
87	
88	**Broken lane.** An edge whose upstream end is a park, a failure, or a plain issue no task and
89	no PR names is drawn as a dashed line in the critical hue with a `»` break, and the downstream
90	text says why in words. A lane is not broken because it waits: a future `Not-before` is the
91	mechanism working.
92	
93	## The Scheduled group — a task × day grid
94	
95	One row per scheduled task, one cell per day column, at the day's anchor. A cell's state is
96	carried by **form and the semantic set**, so it reads in either theme:
97	
98	| State | Cell | Read from |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| **ran** | filled, good | a closed item of that task with `outcome:done` / `delivered`, by `closed_at` |
101	| **asked, declined** | hollow, muted | a closed item with `outcome:obsolete`, or the schedule board's `verdict: no` for that ask |
102	| **parked** | filled, amber | an open item of that task at `needs-human-approval` (it waits for a person) |
103	| **failure park** | hatched, critical stroke | an open item at `needs-human-failure`, placed on the day it parked; `◂` at the left edge when older than the window |
104	| **predicted** | hollow, the machine's blue | the next anchor for a task whose last verdict on the board was `go` or `fail-open` |

input.body:
The whole redesign (#1602), all five phases. Phases 1–2 are the **data**; 3–5 are the **pages** drawn from it.

Phase 1 goes first because its counters accumulate from the day they ship: every page built on them renders a named gap until a member's fold carries them, so the pages cannot lead.

## Phase 1 — the usage fold's new counters (#1603)

Each field follows the file's own rules: a tuple against the `fields` header, **no key where the source could not answer**, a week row grown from the first day that carried it.

| Field | What it carries |
|---|---|
| `tokensByModel` | the same spend split per model, the four counters kept apart so a day is priceable per counter |
| `humanSeconds` / `agentSeconds` | how the sessions' wall clock divided — each turn billed the gap that produced it |
| `prs` | each merged PR's `leadHours`, `issueLeadHours`, `sessionToMergeHours`, past a new `prsFoldedThrough` watermark |
| `taskCost` | `sessions`/`tokensIn`/`tokensOut`/`userMessages` per task |
| `parks` | how often each task needed a human, by kind |
| `ruleTokensByPack` | where a session's rule-token weight came from |

Plus the worker **deepens its shallow checkout** over the day window, so the line counts stop being unknown for every day but today.

Three decisions worth reading: `prs` carries **durations, never percentiles** (a week's p50 is not derivable from its days'); the human-second **cap is declared in the file's own `caps` header**, so the floor is never guessed; and **parks are read from label events**, since an item's final labels say only where it ended.

## Phase 2 — the page-side reads (#1604)

Every figure is a reduction over a response the page already fetches — **the viewer makes no new request**. Merged PRs kept in the projection with `merged_at` and `closesIssue` parsed before the body is dropped; `pricing.mjs` keeping *a number*, *unpriced* and *a priced sum beside an unpriced remainder* strictly apart; the scheduler heartbeat topped up from the fold's hour tier as a floor, so a scheduler older than one page of runs stops reading as one that never ran.

## Phase 3 — the fleet page's top block (#1605)

One ruled sheet, a stub column naming five bands, **no cards**, figures in mono on fixed tracks, and exactly one warm object — the Start-here slip. It replaced the benefits tiles, the glance tiles and two of the four activity charts; each fact moved to where it is acted on.

`fleet-ledger.mjs` **decides** — the window, the three unknown states, each figure's own *bad when*, so a figure with no number carries the sentence saying why and a quotient inherits both its inputs' gaps. `sheet.mjs` **renders** — one function per mark, the heartbeat, wake strip, pulse and sparklines all the same square at four scales.

**The wake strip states an absence.** A task's anchor lives in its own declaration, and a fleet read carries task *paths*, not contents; fetching them is one request per task per member. An empty strip reads as *nothing wakes* — the serious verdict — so the cell says it was not read.

## Phase 4 — the repo page's block and the Work board (#1606)

The block is the fleet's ledger one member deep, with a machine that asks a different question one level down: its heartbeat is one square per **hour**, beside CI on main, whose failing state is the one critical on the block. `repo-ledger.mjs` adds the three questions only a repo can ask — the queue's own outcome **words** (an obsolete share; `none` above zero meaning items closed without converging at all), this repo's corpus weight against the fleet mean, and the per-task expand with tokens-per-close beside the model each task runs on.

**The board.** The lane is the flow: a row is a connected component of the `Blocked-by` / `Ends-when` / `Closes` graph — never one task (that hides the chain: an approval park is nothing without the PR it holds) and never one kind (that puts the two ends of one edge in different rows, and the edge *is* the finding).

Three placements are its whole argument: a stamped `Not-before` **is** the schedule; a relative one is **flagged rather than guessed**, because it is a date the machine will treat as absent; and a plain issue nobody is scheduled to close gives its downstream item **no time at all** — drawn as a broken lane, and said in words.

The Scheduled group is a task × day grid where a failure park lands on its **own task's row**, so a hatched cell followed by filled ones is the record disagreeing with the roster's held-lane claim, read left to right on one line.

## Phase 5 — the explore panels (#1607)

One per status, because the reader's next move differs by status, and every one ends in a single imperative. Every field names its source; a field the page cannot read says **not read** rather than being omitted — a PR's size, the checks on its head sha, a `Refs` edge, each of which costs a request per mark. The converge command they print is spelled as `converge-item.mjs`'s own usage block spells it.

## What each folder changed

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/usage-fold/
  the counters: vocabularies and the caps/prsFoldedThrough header in
  usage-format.mjs, extraction and folding in fold-usage.mjs, the parks read in
  read-queue.mjs, a new read-prs.mjs with its pure derivations in pr-fields.mjs,
  and the history deepen in worker.mjs

packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/
  a new pull-requests.mjs publishing those derivations — from the pure module,
  since the consumer is a page that runs in a browser

packs/claudinite-dashboard/
  new: pricing.mjs, fleet-ledger.mjs, sheet.mjs, repo-ledger.mjs, board.mjs,
  board-view.mjs, explore.mjs.  cache.mjs and github.mjs keep merged PRs;
  fleet.mjs tops the heartbeat up from the fold; fleet-growth.mjs gains the
  fleet mean; model.mjs gains wakeStrip; view-fleet.mjs and view-repo.mjs
  render the sheets and the board and drop what moved; index.html carries the
  identity's palette and the board's marks; config.mjs and build-site.mjs
  carry `rates`

engine/pack_loader/
  session-summary.mjs prints a per-pack split of the rule-token weight

packs/claudinite-dashboard/docs/
  five corrections the implementation found in the spec
```

## Spec corrections

- **`fields.parks`** is the imported `PARK_KINDS`, not a re-spelled list whose order contradicted the file's own rule.
- **The per-pack rule-token facet** loses its thousands separators: the facets are comma-joined, so a comma must stay the segment's terminator.
- **`merged_at`** rides each PR's own stub on the issues endpoint; **`closesIssue`** is parsed by the fold's published rule rather than a second one.
- **`Merge:`** is the field the queue writes and `parseWorkItemBody` reads — not `Automerge:` — so that is what the panel names.
- **`Refs #n` is not read**: the PR projection drops the body once the closing issue is out of it, so that edge would cost a request per PR.

## Verification

Both pages were **rendered against fixtures built from this repo's own data** — its usage fold, and for the repo page its 60 open issues, 24 open PRs and 17 task declarations — through a harness driving the actual page, in light and dark.

| Exit condition | Target | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| fleet: members grid marker | above 900 px @ 1280 | **683 px** |
| repo: Work board begins | above 900 px @ 1280 | **652 px** |
| repo: top block | ≤ 450 px | **486 px** — the two *not recorded* sentences are wrapped lines where a figure is one; the budget bends before the gap goes unstated |
| every unavailable figure | a named gap | *not recorded — this fold predates humanSeconds*, *no merged PR named a closing issue*, *not read — the anchors are in declarations this page does not fetch* |

The board found a real one on this repo while being verified: **#1609's lane is broken — nobody is scheduled to close #1606** — drawn dashed in the critical hue with the finding in words and the panel's imperative under it.

Full suite green: **3,086 tests, 0 failures**. `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` at 0 blocking, with six new advisories, all `file-placement` on cross-pack `shared-code` reaches — the same standing every other dashboard module importing it already has.

Closes #1605
Closes #1606
Closes #1607
Refs #1602

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.

- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and author the canon packs those facets earn. Use from a canon when a project's evidence shows a facet its shelf does not yet home — the curation stages' pack-writing method, and an owner's when asking what a project has taught the shelf.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- improve-comments: Improve the comments in a repo's own source — delete the ones that restate the code or narrate a past edit, correct the ones that have drifted from what the code now does, and add the why where only a reader's guess carries it. Use when working a repo's comments as their own pass (the tidy-repo pack's improve-comments task), never as a side effect of another change.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- production-retrospective: Design and file the review that comes back on its own once a larger element has lived in production long enough to judge — is it working, misused, overused, underused — read from its real production record against expectations written down when the element was designed. Use when designing a larger element (the brief is authored then), when filing a migration plan's chain (the retrospective is its last link), when a merge completes a design-doc'd element, or when defining a new retrospective class for a pack, a repo, or the fleet.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. - writing-handover-issues: How to write a task list a PERSON will execute — a handover issue, an adoption checklist, a "steps only a human can do" list. - writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-pack-prose: How pack prose is written — RULES.md rules, SKILL.md bodies and check text in a Claudinite pack, local or canon — brevity, structure, triggerability, findability, and the per-pack references doc that carries each rule's rationale. Use before writing or editing any pack's RULES.md or SKILL.md, or when landing a lesson as prose.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. - artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

{"number":1616,"title":"Dashboard redesign: the fleet ledger, the repo page and the Work board","body":"The whole redesign (#1602), all five phases. Phases 1–2 are the **data**; 3–5 are the **pages** drawn from it.

Phase 1 goes first because its counters accumulate from the day they ship: every page built on them renders a named gap until a member's fold carries them, so the pages cannot lead.

## Phase 1 — the usage fold's new counters (#1603)

Each field follows the file's own rules: a tuple against the `fields` header, **no key where the source could not answer**, a week row grown from the first day that carried it.

| Field | What it carries |
|---|---|
| `tokensByModel` | the same spend split per model, the four counters kept apart so a day is priceable per counter |
| `humanSeconds` / `agentSeconds` | how the sessions' wall clock divided — each turn billed the gap that produced it |
| `prs` | each merged PR's `leadHours`, `issueLeadHours`, `sessionToMergeHours`, past a new `prsFoldedThrough` watermark |
| `taskCost` | `sessions`/`tokensIn`/`tokensOut`/`userMessages` per task |
| `parks` | how often each task needed a human, by kind |
| `ruleTokensByPack` | where a session's rule-token weight came from |

Plus the worker **deepens its shallow checkout** over the day window, so the line counts stop being unknown for every day but today.

Three decisions worth reading: `prs` carries **durations, never percentiles** (a week's p50 is not derivable from its days'); the human-second **cap is declared in the file's own `caps` header**, so the floor is never guessed; and **parks are read from label events**, since an item's final labels say only where it ended.

## Phase 2 — the page-side reads (#1604)

Every figure is a reduction over a response the page already fetches — **the viewer makes no new request**. Merged PRs kept in the projection with `merged_at` and `closesIssue` parsed before the body is dropped; `pricing.mjs` keeping *a number*, *unpriced* and *a priced sum beside an unpriced remainder* strictly apart; the scheduler heartbeat topped up from the fold's hour tier as a floor, so a scheduler older than one page of runs stops reading as one that never ran.

## Phase 3 — the fleet page's top block (#1605)

One ruled sheet, a stub column naming five bands, **no cards**, figures in mono on fixed tracks, and exactly one warm object — the Start-here slip. It replaced the benefits tiles, the glance tiles and two of the four activity charts; each fact moved to where it is acted on.

`fleet-ledger.mjs` **decides** — the window, the three unknown states, each figure's own *bad when*, so a figure with no number carries the sentence saying why and a quotient inherits both its inputs' gaps. `sheet.mjs` **renders** — one function per mark, the heartbeat, wake strip, pulse and sparklines all the same square at four scales.

**The wake strip states an absence.** A task's anchor lives in its own declaration, and a fleet read carries task *paths*, not contents; fetching them is one request per task per member. An empty strip reads as *nothing wakes* — the serious verdict — so the cell says it was not read.

## Phase 4 — the repo page's block and the Work board (#1606)

The block is the fleet's ledger one member deep, with a machine that asks a different question one level down: its heartbeat is one square per **hour**, beside CI on main, whose failing state is the one critical on the block. `repo-ledger.mjs` adds the three questions only a repo can ask — the queue's own outcome **words** (an obsolete share; `none` above zero meaning items closed without converging at all), this repo's corpus weight against the fleet mean, and the per-task expand with tokens-per-close beside the model each task runs on.

**The board.** The lane is the flow: a row is a connected component of the `Blocked-by` / `Ends-when` / `Closes` graph — never one task (that hides the chain: an approval park is nothing without the PR it holds) and never one kind (that puts the two ends of one edge in different rows, and the edge *is* the finding).

Three placements are its whole argument: a stamped `Not-before` **is** the schedule; a relative one is **flagged rather than guessed**, because it is a date the machine will treat as absent; and a plain issue nobody is scheduled to close gives its downstream item **no time at all** — drawn as a broken lane, and said in words.

The Scheduled group is a task × day grid where a failure park lands on its **own task's row**, so a hatched cell followed by filled ones is the record disagreeing with the roster's held-lane claim, read left to right on one line.

## Phase 5 — the explore panels (#1607)

One per status, because the reader's next move differs by status, and every one ends in a single imperative. Every field names its source; a field the page cannot read says **not read** rather than being omitted — a PR's size, the checks on its head sha, a `Refs` edge, each of which costs a request per mark. The converge command they print is spelled as `converge-item.mjs`'s own usage block spells it.

## What each folder changed

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/usage-fold/
  the counters: vocabularies and the caps/prsFoldedThrough header in
  usage-format.mjs, extraction and folding in fold-usage.mjs, the parks read in
  read-queue.mjs, a new read-prs.mjs with its pure derivations in pr-fields.mjs,
  and the history deepen in worker.mjs

packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/
  a new pull-requests.mjs publishing those derivations — from the pure module,
  since the consumer is a page that runs in a browser

packs/claudinite-dashboard/
  new: pricing.mjs, fleet-ledger.mjs, sheet.mjs, repo-ledger.mjs, board.mjs,
  board-view.mjs, explore.mjs.  cache.mjs and github.mjs keep merged PRs;
  fleet.mjs tops the heartbeat up from the fold; fleet-growth.mjs gains the
  fleet mean; model.mjs gains wakeStrip; view-fleet.mjs and view-repo.mjs
  render the sheets and the board and drop what moved; index.html carries the
  identity's palette and the board's marks; config.mjs and build-site.mjs
  carry `rates`

engine/pack_loader/
  session-summary.mjs prints a per-pack split of the rule-token weight

packs/claudinite-dashboard/docs/
  five corrections the implementation found in the spec
```

## Spec corrections

- **`fields.parks`** is the imported `PARK_KINDS`, not a re-spelled list whose order contradicted the file's own rule.
- **The per-pack rule-token facet** loses its thousands separators: the facets are comma-joined, so a comma must stay the segment's terminator.
- **`merged_at`** rides each PR's own stub on the issues endpoint; **`closesIssue`** is parsed by the fold's published rule rather than a second one.
- **`Merge:`** is the field the queue writes and `parseWorkItemBody` reads — not `Automerge:` — so that is what the panel names.
- **`Refs #n` is not read**: the PR projection drops the body once the closing issue is out of it, so that edge would cost a request per PR.

## Verification

Both pages were **rendered against fixtures built from this repo's own data** — its usage fold, and for the repo page its 60 open issues, 24 open PRs and 17 task declarations — through a harness driving the actual page, in light and dark.

| Exit condition | Target | Measured |
|---|---|---|
| fleet: members grid marker | above 900 px @ 1280 | **683 px** |
| repo: Work board begins | above 900 px @ 1280 | **652 px** |
| repo: top block | ≤ 450 px | **486 px** — the two *not recorded* sentences are wrapped lines where a figure is one; the budget bends before the gap goes unstated |
| every unavailable figure | a named gap | *not recorded — this fold predates humanSeconds*, *no merged PR named a closing issue*, *not read — the anchors are in declarations this page does not fetch* |

The board found a real one on this repo while being verified: **#1609's lane is broken — nobody is scheduled to close #1606** — drawn dashed in the critical hue with the finding in words and the panel's imperative under it.

Full suite green: **3,086 tests, 0 failures**. `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` at 0 blocking, with six new advisories, all `file-placement` on cross-pack `shared-code` reaches — the same standing every other dashboard module importing it already has.

Closes #1603
Closes #1604
Closes #1605
Closes #1606
Closes #1607
Refs #1602

Three placements are its whole argument: a stamped `Not-before` **is** the schedule; a relative one is **flagged rather than guessed**, because it is a date the machine will treat as absent; and a plain issue nobody is scheduled to close gives its downstream item **no time at all** — drawn as a broken lane, and said in words.

The Scheduled group is a task × day grid where a failure park lands on its **own task's row**, so a hatched cell followed by filled ones is the record disagreeing with the roster's held-lane claim, read left to right on one line.

## Phase 5 — the explore panels (#1607)

One per status, because the reader's next move differs by status, and every one ends in a single imperative. Every field names its source; a field the page cannot read says **not read** rather than being omitted — a PR's size, the checks on its head sha, a `Refs` edge, each of which costs a request per mark. The converge command they print is spelled as `converge-item.mjs`'s own usage block spells it.

## What each folder changed

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/tasks/usage-fold/
  the counters: vocabularies and the caps/prsFoldedThrough header in
  usage-format.mjs, extraction and folding in fold-usage.mjs, the parks read in
  read-queue.mjs, a new read-prs.mjs with its pure derivations in pr-fields.mjs,
  and the history deepen in worker.mjs

packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/
  a new pull-requests.mjs publishing those derivations — from the pure module,
  since the consumer is a page that runs in a browser

packs/claudinite-dashboard/
  new: pricing.mjs, fleet-ledger.mjs, sheet.mjs, repo-ledger.mjs, board.mjs,
  board-view.mjs, explore.mjs.  cache.mjs and github.mjs keep merged PRs;
  fleet.mjs tops the heartbeat up from the fold; fleet-growth.mjs gains the
  fleet mean; model.mjs gains wakeStrip; view-fleet.mjs and view-repo.mjs
  render the sheets and the board and drop what moved; index.html carries the
  identity's palette and the board's marks; config.mjs and build-site.mjs
  carry `rates`

engine/pack_loader/
  session-summary.mjs prints a per-pack split of the rule-token weight

packs/claudinite-dashboard/docs/
  five corrections the implementation found in the spec
```

**The sign-in surface is untouched.** `auth.mjs`, `oauth-exchange.mjs`, `deployment-config.mjs` and the deploy task carry no change, and index.html's sign-in markup is byte-identical to `main`'s — the only new config key, `rates`, travels the declaration path beside `canonRepo`, not the repository-variable path the sign-in pair uses. The `data-info` disclosure pairs match `main` exactly apart from `repo-tiles-2`, which went with the tiles it explained.

## Spec corrections

- **`fields.parks`** is the imported `PARK_KINDS`, not a re-spelled list whose order contradicted the file's own rule.
- **The per-pack rule-token facet** loses its thousands separators: the facets are comma-joined, so a comma must stay the segment's terminator.
- **`merged_at`** rides each PR's own stub on the issues endpoint; **`closesIssue`** is parsed by the fold's published rule rather than a second one.
- **`Merge:`** is the field the queue writes and `parseWorkItemBody` reads — not `Automerge:` — so that is what the panel names.
- **`Refs #n` is not read**: the PR projection drops the body once the closing issue is out of it, so that edge would cost a request per PR.

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
